data.cultural_impact: Sugreev is a significant figure in Hindu mythology, particularly in the epic Ramayana. He is the king of the Vanara (monkey) tribe and was a central figure in helping Lord Rama locate and rescue his wife, Sita, who had been abducted by the demon king Ravana. Sugreev's cleverness and strength played a crucial role in the eventual victory of good over evil.
data.spiritual_significance: Sugreev represents the power of intelligence and wisdom in overcoming challenges. His name itself translates to 'one who has a good mind,' reflecting the importance of mental acuity in Hindu philosophy. Sugreev's dedication to helping Lord Rama reaffirms the value of selflessness and devotion to dharma (duty). Furthermore, his ability to unite the various monkey tribes in the pursuit of Sita signifies the power of unity and harmony in achieving spiritual and moral goals.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sugreev, in Hindu mythology, symbolizes the triumph of inner wisdom and courage over physical limitations. He was born with the ability to see in the dark but was afflicted with a curse that left him incapable of ruling his kingdom. Yet, he overcame this challenge through his intelligence and valor, ultimately reclaiming his kingdom and becoming a revered king.

vedic_reference.note: Well-known name in Hindu mythology and is mentioned in various Vedic scriptures. It is the name of the king of the Vanara (monkey) tribe in the Indian epic Ramayana.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Sugreev was the king of the Vanaras, a race of monkey-like beings in Hindu mythology. The name Sugreev carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

trends: Sugreev is a popular name for boys in India
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Sugreev remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.
